phases.title: Dogfood: agent-flow runs on itself
phases.goal: The repo is planned, remembered and gated with its own loop; the first friction found is fixed.

tasks.title: Commit the agent-flow setup for this repo

acceptance.text: agent-flow doctor and doctor --tokens are green for this repo
REQUIREMENTS.md carries the v0.11 ids and plan validate has no warnings
Friction found during setup is recorded in .memory/events.jsonl (tag dogfood)
.claude/settings.local.json is ignored and not committed

tasks.title: init: honest .gitignore label and ignore Claude Code local settings

acceptance.text: ensureGitignore reports 'appended' (new status) when it only adds entries, 'skipped' when none are missing; never 'overwritten'
init --claude adds .claude/settings.local.json to .gitignore alongside the scratch entries
doctor --tokens '.gitignore covers agent-flow scratch' check accepts the new entry set

phases.title: Project detection beyond five frameworks
phases.goal: onboard, AGENTS.md and context packs describe plain Node/TS, Python, Go, Rust and monorepo projects correctly.

tasks.title: Detect plain Node/TypeScript projects, test runners, lint and typecheck

acceptance.text: A package.json without a known framework yields stack 'Node' (plus 'TypeScript' when tsconfig.json or typescript dep exists), never 'none'
Test runner is detected from devDependencies or the test script: vitest, jest, node:test, mocha
lint and typecheck commands are detected from scripts (lint, eslint, typecheck, type-check, tsc) and from eslint/tsconfig presence when no script exists
Package manager falls back to packageManager field in package.json, then to npm when package.json exists without a lockfile
This repo onboarded reports pnpm, Node + TypeScript, vitest, typecheck

tasks.title: Detect Python, Go and Rust projects with their commands

acceptance.text: pyproject.toml / requirements.txt yields stack Python with test (pytest), lint (ruff/flake8 when configured) and the detected package manager (uv, poetry, pip)
go.mod yields stack Go with go test ./..., go vet ./..., go build ./...
Cargo.toml yields stack Rust with cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo build
Gate resolution uses the detected commands when config has none for a gate name

tasks.title: List monorepo workspaces as packages with their own commands

acceptance.text: pnpm-workspace.yaml, package.json workspaces and turbo.json are recognized; each package is listed with name, path and its own test/build/lint/typecheck commands
PROJECT.md and AGENTS.md generated sections include a Workspaces table when packages exist
A context pack for a task whose scope lies inside one package names that package and its commands first

phases.title: Router feedback from observed usage
phases.goal: Judge the router from what tasks actually cost and how often they passed first time; suggest, never apply.

tasks.title: agent-flow router report: per-tier outcomes from task-stats and usage

acceptance.text: task-stats.json records, per task, the tier and rung assigned at each gate run (not only counts), so outcomes can be grouped by tier
router report prints, per tier: tasks routed, first-attempt green rate, escalations, median tokens per task (from usage subagent data when available, 'n/a' otherwise)
--json emits the same data; --all aggregates every project usage can see
A project with no gate history prints a clear 'no routed tasks yet' line and exits 0

tasks.title: Verdict and threshold suggestion in the router report

acceptance.text: Report flags 'optimistic' when more than a third of light/standard tasks escalated, 'pessimistic' when more than two thirds of deep tasks passed on the first attempt, 'balanced' otherwise; thresholds are documented
The suggestion is a concrete config change (orchestration.router.thresholds values) printed as text; the command never writes config.json
Verdicts need at least five routed tasks; below that the report says the sample is too small

phases.title: Published benchmark
phases.goal: The 24% claim becomes a reproducible table across three tasks, three workflows and both runtimes.

acceptance.text: Seed repo with package.json and a failing-by-absence feature; task.md asks for POST /shorten and GET /:slug persisted to a JSON file

Hidden tests cover the happy path and the table-stakes criteria: body cap, scheme allowlist, atomic write, concurrent writes serialized, a missing data file on first boot yields an empty store, crypto-grade slugs
test/bench-tasks.test.ts validates every bench/tasks/* folder: bench.json parses, check command present, seed/ and hidden/ exist
task.md asks for a CLI that reads CSV from a file or stdin and prints per-column count/min/max/mean with --json; hidden tests exercise malformed rows, empty input, exit codes
bench.json check runs the hidden tests with node --test

tasks.title: Bench task: refactor existing code without changing behaviour

acceptance.text: Seed contains a working but tangled order-pricing module with its own passing tests; task.md asks to split it into pure functions and add discount rules
Hidden tests pin existing behaviour (golden outputs) and verify the new rules

tasks.title: Run the matrix and publish docs/bench-results.md

acceptance.text: Three runs per task × variant (plain, gsd, agent-flow) × runtime (claude, codex); bench report --out docs/bench-results.md
docs/bench-results.md states models, agent-flow version, dates and the exact commands; README links it and replaces the single-e2e 24% sentence with the table's numbers
